summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to export data to separate ML systems. Capabilities range from in-database model training (BigQuery ML, Redshift ML, Aurora ML) to managed LLM functions and vector search (Snowflake Cortex, Databricks Mosaic AI, MongoDB Atlas). Native vector search support is now a key differentiator, with some platforms offering built-in indexing and others relying on extensions like pgvector.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Document AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs (from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, OpenAI and others) via SQL and Python functions for tasks like summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, and text generation. Cortex Search offers a managed retrieval service, and Cortex Analyst enables natural-language querying of structured data. Snowflake also extends Cortex capabilities to its managed Postgres offering.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE/VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARity functions and provides the fully managed Cortex Search service for semantic/hybrid retrieval. Snowflake Postgres also integrates Cortex for AI/vector workflows.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated — managed, serverless access to multiple third-party foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, etc.) callable directly through SQL/Python; supports fine-tuning and RAG via Cortex Search.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits. Cortex LLM functions are charged per token processed (varies by model), and Cortex Search/serverless features incur compute and storage costs. No separate license; usage added to standard account billing.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-database ML) with Vertex AI integration and Gemini models
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization, and more) using SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call remote models including Gemini and embedding models (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING) directly from SQL, enabling generative AI and inference at scale.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search. BigQuery supports the VECTOR_SEARCH function along with CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings stored in tables.
databases.llm_integration: Strong — via Vertex AI remote models, BigQuery can invoke Gemini and PaLM-based models and embedding models directly in SQL for generation, summarization, and RAG workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML charges for query/compute (on-demand per TB scanned or capacity slots) plus model creation/training costs. Calls to Vertex AI remote models (Gemini, embeddings) incur separate Vertex AI inference charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database AI/LLM calls
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type with similarity operators and ANN indexing (HNSW, IVFFlat), while pgai (from Timescale) adds functions to generate embeddings and call LLMs (OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic, etc.) directly from SQL. Together they enable RAG and semantic search within a standard Postgres database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL — vector search is provided exclusively via the third-party pgvector extension, which must be installed and enabled. Once enabled, pgvector offers robust HNSW/IVFFlat indexing, but it is not part of the base engine.
databases.llm_integration: Available through extensions such as pgai, which adds SQL functions to call external LLM providers for embeddings and text generation; not built into core Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; pgvector and pgai carry no license cost. Expenses derive from hosting/compute (self-managed or managed services like Timescale, Supabase, Neon) plus any external LLM API usage fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — in-database inference via Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend
databases.description: Aurora ML enables SQL queries to call out to AWS ML services for predictions directly from the database. It integrates with Amazon SageMaker for custom models, Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis, and Amazon Bedrock for foundation-model inference, allowing inference results to be used inline in queries without building separate pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora ML itself does not provide vector search. Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can support vector search only via the pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML feature; MySQL-compatible Aurora lacks native pgvector support. Thus Aurora ML has no built-in vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Yes — via integration with Amazon Bedrock, Aurora ML can invoke foundation models/LLMs from SQL, and via Comprehend for NLP tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage costs plus the usage charges of the invoked AWS services (SageMaker, Comprehend, or Bedrock).

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — in-warehouse model creation and inference using SQL and Amazon SageMaker/Bedrock
databases.description: Redshift ML lets analysts create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, with Amazon SageMaker Autopilot handling model training behind the scenes. Models can then be used for in-database prediction functions. It also supports integration with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI and with pre-trained SageMaker models.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector search as part of Redshift ML. Redshift has introduced broader vector capabilities separately, but the Redshift ML service focuses on model training/inference, not vector similarity search; treat vector search as not supported within this feature.
databases.llm_integration: Yes — Redshift ML supports invoking Amazon Bedrock large language models from SQL for generative AI tasks, in addition to SageMaker-trained models.
databases.pricing_notes: Training via SageMaker incurs SageMaker charges; prediction functions run within Redshift compute (no extra inference fee for local models). Standard Redshift cluster/serverless costs apply, plus Bedrock usage when LLMs are called.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform through Mosaic AI, covering model fine-tuning, serving, foundation model APIs, and agent frameworks, tightly integrated with the Lakehouse and Unity Catalog governance. Databricks Vector Search offers a managed vector database that automatically syncs embeddings from Delta tables for RAG and semantic search.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in managed vector search. Databricks Vector Search is a first-party service that indexes embeddings and supports automatic syncing from Delta tables, with serverless querying integrated into the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Extensive — Mosaic AI Foundation Model APIs provide access to open and proprietary LLMs (Llama, DBRX, Anthropic via partnerships), with support for fine-tuning, serving, and building RAG/agent applications.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs). Vector Search, model serving, and Foundation Model APIs are billed by compute/throughput or per-token for pay-per-token foundation model endpoints.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic search and RAG within MongoDB
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational documents and performing approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search using an aggregation-pipeline ($vectorSearch) interface. It supports hybrid search combining vector and traditional queries, making it well suited for RAG applications on operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search within MongoDB Atlas. It is a managed feature of Atlas (built on Lucene/HNSW indexing) accessed via the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, not an external extension.
databases.llm_integration: Integration-friendly rather than built-in LLM hosting — Atlas pairs with external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, LangChain, LlamaIndex) to generate embeddings and power RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas clusters; vector search runs on Atlas Search nodes. Costs are tied to the Atlas cluster tier and dedicated Search node resources; embedding generation via third-party LLM providers is billed separately.
